2. The predecessors of respondent Nos. 1(a) to 1(c), 2 and 3 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 75 of 1984 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Barisal for declaration of title to the suit land. Subsequently by amendment of the plaint the plaintiffs prayed for recovery of khas possession. In the suit the predecessor of the petitioners and respondent Nos. 4 to 13 were impleaded as defendants. 

 3. The plaint case, in short, was that the laud measuring 1912 decimals appertaining to mouza Bagura Alekanda in J.L. No. 50 under C.S. Khatian Nos. 160 and 178, plot No. 1548 belonged to Gobinda Chandra Shil. He executed a will and appointed his wife Sona Lakhahmi as executrix. Defendant No. 3, Ramesh Chandra Shil was the next reversioner. After death of Gobinda Chandra Shil, Sona Lakhshmi obtained probate in Probate Case No. 6 of 1917 filed before the District Judge, Barisal. Sona Lakhshmi and the reversionary heir leased out the said land to Dinabandhu Gangopadhya (father of defendant Nos. 1and 2) by patta dated 05.11.1941 for legal necessity and delivered Possession thereof. In the said patta by mistake plot No. 1549 was written instead of plot No. 1548, but the boundaries and the area of the land were correctly written. Since the said pattan defendant Nos. 1 and 2 had been residing on the suit land constructing dwelling structures thereon and on payment of rent, municipal tax etc. The said defendants transferred the suit property to the plaintiffs by a registered sale deed dated 12.05 1970, but in that sale deed also mistakenly plot No. 1549 was written in lieu of plot No. 1548. During R.S. operation the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of defendant No. 3 and her mother Sona Lakhshmi although they had never claimed the same. Husband of defendant No. 6 in collusion with Sudhir Chandra Dutta, an employee of defendant No. 5 constructed structures on plot No. 804, and as such, the plaint was amended incorporating prayer for recovery of khas possession in respect of 'Kha' schedule land. The collusively prepared wrong record in the name of No. 3 and her mother has clouded title of the plaintiffs in the suit land and hence the suit. 

 4. Defendant No. 6 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the plaint case and contending, inter-alia, that Sona Lakhshmi Shil and her next reversioner did not execute and register the alleged patta dated 05.11.1941 in favour of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and no such patty was acted upon. Dinobundhu Gangopadhya or his heirs defendant Nos. 1 and 2 never possessed the suit land. The land of C.S. Plot No. 1549 has been recorded in R.S. Plot No. 798-803/2001/2004. Manindra and others owned the suit land in Mirash ejara right. Plot No. 1548 was possessed by temporary lessees of Sona Lakhshmi, named Bipin Bihari, Abdul Aziz, Hiron Kumar Karmakar and three others. Defendant No. 5 attempted to acquire the land of temporary tenant Abdul Aziz. When landlord Ramesh Chandra Shil attempted to make the land khas defendant No. 5 took settlement on 29.12.1945 in Mirash ejara right of the land of plot Na.1548 and as he failed to get khas possession of the entire property, he gradually purchased the interests of temporary tenants and obtained khas possession of the suit land. Defendant No. 5 made constructions in the Suit land, opened municipal holding and mutated the property in his name and in the name of his wife and inducted tenants therein on monthly rental basis. Defendant No. 5 and his wife transferred 0.431 acre of land including the suit land to defendant No. 6 by a registered sale deed dated 01.09.1969 at a consideration of TK.6,000.00. After purchase defendant No. 6 mutated her name in the revenue records and in the municipality in respect of the purchased land and constructing structures thereon she has been possessing some part of the suit land herself along with the members of her family and some parts through the monthly tenants. The plaintiffs have no title, interest and possession in the suit land, and they have filed the suit to grab the same creating forged paper and as such, the suit was liable to be dismissed.
